$description: Structured extraction of bilateral FX pair analysis from two base currency dossiers plus web research

pair_convention.spot_explanation: CAD/CHF at 0.58554 means 1 CAD = 0.58554 CHF. Rising = CAD strengthening vs CHF. Both source dossiers are written in inverted conventions relative to this pair — the CAD dossier in USD/CAD (rising = weaker CAD) and the CHF dossier in USD/CHF and EUR/CHF (rising = weaker CHF) — so every stance in this report is expressed in CAD/CHF pair terms.
pair_convention.base_dossier_tactical_stance: Neutral CAD tactically, conviction 2, net score +0.001
pair_convention.quote_dossier_tactical_stance: Bearish CHF tactically, conviction 3, net score −0.2358

executive_summary: CAD/CHF trades at 0.58554 (gated store close, 2026-09-03), meaning one Canadian dollar buys 0.58554 Swiss francs, and the pair has risen 1.65% over one month, 2.41% over three months, 2.02% over six months and 2.42% over twelve — a uniformly Canadian-dollar-positive scorecard achieved almost entirely in the last eight weeks. The dominant bilateral narrative is the simplest in the G10: a +225bp policy differential between a Bank of Canada at 2.25% and a Swiss National Bank at 0.00%, held against a counterparty whose own conditional inflation forecast is conditioned on that zero rate through 2028, and which has told the market twice since June that it will lean against franc appreciation and never against franc weakness. Bilateral research adds a genuinely new flow dynamic that neither standalone dossier captures: following US-Japanese intervention in the yen, hedge fund investors are looking beyond the yen for carry-trade funding currencies, with the franc emerging as the beneficiary, and over the past two weeks hedge funds have halved their net short yen positions while net short franc positions have climbed to a two-month high — a structural rotation that makes CAD/CHF a primary beneficiary rather than an incidental one. The counter-evidence arrived after the valuation date and deserves naming up front: Swiss August CPI jumped to 0.8% year-on-year against a 0.5% consensus, the fastest since August 2024, with core accelerating to 0.4% from 0.3% — its first increase this year, and Q2 GDP expanded 1.9%, its strongest quarterly growth in five years and above the 1.6% consensus. The settled direction verdict is tactically Bullish at conviction 3 (score +0.349) and strategically Neutral at conviction 2 (score +0.029), and the price payload is consistent with it — the pair sits at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week closing range with a fully bullish-stacked 50/100/200-day moving-average configuration and a clean sequence of higher highs and higher lows since early July. The caveat is entry, not direction: the 52-week high of 0.58783 was set one session before the payload spot, the nearest computed resistance band carries only two touches, and above 0.58738 there is a 305-pip structural void with no computed zone at all — a setup with no overhead supply and no cushion beneath it either.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no PPP level available for this cross. On relative BIS real effective rates the Canadian dollar is the cheap leg: Canada's broad real effective index is 95.71 for June 2026 against Switzerland's 101.69, placing CAD roughly 5.9% below CHF, with the Canadian index down 3.41 points over twelve months against a Swiss decline of only 1.03 points. Both readings are June 2026 vintages, approximately 63 days from the valuation date, with Canada at an estimated 15th percentile of its trailing range and Switzerland at the 40th percentile of a 30-month window. The pair's own long-run position is the counterweight: spot at 0.58554 sits 407 pips (6.5%) below the 200-week moving average of 0.62619, which is still declining at 0.000848 per week, with 199 consecutive weeks without a close above it. What is priced at 0.58554 is a currency pair that is expensive against its own last twelve months and cheap against its own last four years. The multi-year record is unambiguous: CAD/CHF traded near 0.6532 in 2023 and near 0.7463 in 2022, so the structural direction of this cross has been down, driven by persistently lower Swiss inflation forcing continuous real franc appreciation — a mechanism the August Swiss CPI print of 0.8% headline and 0.4% core begins, marginally, to erode.

market_context.recent_regime: The 130-bar window divides into two regimes: a rectangle-bound grind from March through mid-June with subdued realised volatility and no directional conviction, followed by a complete change of character from early July, with an unbroken sequence of higher swing lows (0.56511 on 3 July through 0.58447 on 3 September) against higher swing highs (0.58072, 0.58648, 0.58783). The pair set its 52-week high and 52-week closing high on 2 September, the day the Bank of Canada held at 2.25% with a mildly hawkish tilt, then gave back 17 pips on 3 September as Swiss CPI and GDP data landed. The dominant narrative underneath is carry: the lack of central bank support, divergent monetary policies and the franc's growing use as a funding currency instead of the yen have been pushing the franc crosses higher, with the franc the worst-performing G10 currency so far this quarter.

bilateral_carry_analysis.breakeven_move: CAD/CHF can fall approximately 10 pips over four weeks (0.58554 to 0.5845) and approximately 66 pips over six months (0.58554 to 0.5789) before carry is erased at the policy differential; at the 238.4bp futures roll the figures are 11 pips and 70 pips.
bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The bilateral policy differential is +225bp (BoC 2.25%, SNB 0.00%), with the futures calendar-spread premium of 238.4bp annualised implying roughly 13bp of residual cross-currency basis on top of the differential. On the payload spot of 0.58554, 225bp accrues at roughly 132 pips annualised (140 pips at the futures roll), immaterial against ATR(14) of 30 pips over four weeks but material — worth 2.2 normal days — over six months. Carry-to-volatility is +0.427 against the store's 5.271% three-month estimate, +0.424 against 60-day realised of 5.31%, and +0.358 against 20-day realised of 6.29%, the best risk-adjusted carry available to a long-Canadian-dollar expression anywhere in the G10 on the base dossier's own table (ahead of CAD/JPY's +0.17) and independently ranked the better of the quote dossier's two 225bp franc shorts. The carry regime is working and should persist: the swaps curve fully prices a first SNB hike only in June 2027, outside both horizons in this report, with the SNB having ample room to hold at 0.00% given inflation remains within its mandate.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: High-carry pair: the policy differential is +225bp in the base currency's favour, above the framework's 200bp threshold for boosting Factor 1, and it is the only differential in either dossier where one leg has structurally zero optionality.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral policy differential is +225bp: the Bank of Canada's overnight rate target is 2.25% and the SNB policy rate is 0.00%, the widest positive spread available to the Canadian dollar anywhere in the G10 and the lowest policy rate in the benchmarking set on the quote side. The ten-year differential is +311bp on the payload's own monthly series, both legs as of 2026-06-01 and therefore not live. The trajectory inside four weeks cannot narrow: the gated calendar puts the Bank of Canada at 2026-09-02, where bond markets price a 3% hike probability and all 35 Reuters-polled economists forecast a hold, and the SNB at 2026-09-24, where a hold at zero is close to arithmetic because the June conditional inflation forecast of 0.6%, 0.6% and 0.7% for 2026 to 2028 is explicitly conditioned on the policy rate being 0.00% across the whole three-year horizon. The only paths inside the tactical window are 225bp unchanged or 250bp wider. Transmission is direct and mechanical: this is the textbook carry cross, a low-yielding haven funding a higher-yielding commodity currency, and the store's own futures calendar-spread premium of 238.4bp annualised — the interest differential plus roughly 13bp of unseparable cross-currency basis — is what a rolled position actually pays. Carry-to-vol is +0.43 against the store's 3-month at-the-money estimate of 5.271%, or +0.41 against the 5.46% sixty-day realised carried in the quote dossier, which is the best risk-adjusted carry available to a long-CAD expression in the entire benchmarking set.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market prices both September decisions as holds and prices the 225bp differential in full through the 238.4bp roll, so carry is not free money — it is compensation already quoted. The unpriced element is the asymmetry of the distribution: there is no scheduled path inside four weeks in which this differential narrows.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the differential's floor is what matters more than its ceiling. The gated calendar gives three Bank of Canada decisions against two SNB assessments. On the quote leg there is no realistic path to a higher rate: Swiss headline CPI is 0.4% and core 0.3%, the conditional forecast is pinned at zero through 2028, and Chairman Schlegel has repeatedly cited the undesirable side effects of negative rates. On the base leg the distribution is genuinely two-sided and this is what caps confidence: National Bank and Scotiabank forecast 2.50% in October and 2.75% by December, while BMO, CIBC, RBC and TD forecast no change and Rabobank argues 2.25% is terminal through 2027. The base dossier's own strategic thesis is that roughly 65% of a 2026 Canadian hike bleeds out of the curve at the 2026-10-28 Monetary Policy Report — but that repricing removes 15 to 20bp from the Canadian two-year, not from the policy differential, and against a counterparty stuck at zero a static 225bp is still a positive-carry structure. The genuine strategic risk is a Bank of Canada forced toward a cut by tariff drag. Transmission over this horizon is accrual rather than repricing: 225bp compounds at roughly 66 pips per six months on spot, which is material against an estimated 5.3% annualised volatility.
key_bilateral_metrics: Six-month carry accrual at the 225bp differential: approximately 66 pips on spot 0.58554; approximately 70 pips at the 238.4bp futures roll

BoC Q2 2026 Market Participants Survey median: 2.25% through January 2027, 2.50% in March 2027

Two SNB projection rounds inside the horizon (2026-09-24, 2026-12-10) at which the rate is near-certain to stay at zero
strategic.what_is_priced: Forwards price the differential and nothing else, so the strategic edge is not in the carry level but in the probability that it survives. Consensus is implicitly pricing a Bank of Canada more likely to hike than cut and an SNB that does not move; we agree with the second and take no stronger view than a hold on the first.

factors.horizon_split: Both horizons are Bullish, confidence falling from 68 to 55. Tactically the case is close to arithmetic: two dated decisions, one at a 3% move probability and one at a rate conditioned to stay at zero for three years, so the differential cannot narrow inside the window. Strategically the case becomes a forecast of the Bank of Canada over three meetings, where the six largest Canadian banks split four to two on direction and a tariff-driven cut is a live tail — the floor under the differential is firm because of the quote leg, but the ceiling is genuinely uncertain because of the base leg.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Both economies delivered large simultaneous upside growth surprises in the same six-week window, so the growth-differential channel carries less bilateral information than the default assumes — the surprises largely cancel rather than differentiating.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the factor where the two dossiers look most alike and therefore say least about the pair. Canada printed 3.3% annualised Q2 GDP, a full 80bp above the Bank of Canada's own 2.5% call, with unemployment down to a two-year low of 6.4% and five upside data surprises against three misses in August. Switzerland printed +1.5% quarter-on-quarter on the SECO flash against an AWP consensus of +0.2% to +0.4%, a KOF barometer of 106.7 that is the highest since November 2021, and industrial production of +5.5% year-on-year against a −4.7% forecast. On a quarter-on-quarter basis the Swiss beat is the larger of the two in both magnitude and surprise terms, which neutralises what would otherwise be a Canadian growth-momentum advantage. The inflation differential is enormous and runs the other way: 3.0% Canadian headline against 0.4% Swiss, with Canadian core at 1.9-2.0% against Swiss core at 0.3%. That 260bp headline gap is the fundamental reason the policy differential exists at all, so counting it again here would be double-counting. Both economies also carry the same shape of problem: a Q2 print inflated by pre-tariff activity — Canadian auto and light-truck exports up 27.0% annualised, Swiss chemical and pharmaceutical exports up 25.7% in July ahead of Section 232 taking effect on 2026-07-31 — and both have a dated payback.

Headline CPI: Canada 3.0% versus Switzerland 0.4%; core: Canada 1.9-2.0% versus Switzerland 0.3%
Surprise magnitude: Swiss GDP beat consensus by roughly 110bp and industrial production by 10.2 points; Canada beat the BoC forecast by 80bp
Unemployment: Canada 6.4% (two-year low) versus Switzerland 3.1% registered / 5.07% ILO-harmonised
Both Q2 prints contain tariff front-running: Canadian autos +27.0% annualised, Swiss pharma exports +25.7% in July
tactical.what_is_priced: The market has priced Canada's Q2 beat into roughly 65% odds of a 2026 Bank of Canada hike and has priced the Swiss beat into nothing at all, because it changes no Swiss policy rate — a rates observation rather than a growth-differential one.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Strategically both growth stories decay from here and they decay for the same reason, which is why the differential stays flat. Canada's July advance GDP estimate printed 0.0% before the 2026-08-22 Section 338 duties took effect, and the Bank of Canada's own July projection is 0.7% for 2026, implying materially sub-trend second-half outcomes. Switzerland's Q2 surge is very likely partly pharmaceutical front-running ahead of Section 232 tariffs of up to 15% effective 2026-07-31, with the IMF at 0.8% for 2026 and the SNB at around 1% — both far below the run-rate implied by a +1.5% quarter. The inflation paths also converge in a way that removes rather than creates signal: Canadian headline decays toward the 2.0% core average as the gasoline base effect rolls off, and Swiss inflation is forecast at 0.6% for both 2026 and 2027, so the inflation gap narrows from 260bp toward roughly 150bp without either central bank being moved. There is one genuine long-run asymmetry worth naming and not scoring here: persistently lower Swiss inflation mechanically produces real franc appreciation, a valuation mechanism belonging to the external-balance channel rather than the growth differential.

Tariff exposure: Canadian duties cover 5.2% of exports to the US at 50%; Swiss headline is a variable Section 301 rate up to 12.5% with MFN credit
strategic.what_is_priced: Consensus has accepted the official sub-1% growth path for both economies and marked neither up for its Q2 beat, which we think is correct in both cases; there is no growth-differential edge to price and Neutral is a conclusion rather than a refusal to choose.

factors.horizon_split: Both horizons are Neutral at identical confidence, which is deliberate rather than lazy. Tactically the two economies are surprising positively at the same time and by comparable magnitudes; strategically both decelerate toward sub-1% official forecasts for the same reason, a tariff-driven pull-forward that reverses. The composition of the neutrality changes between horizons — tactically it is two strong prints cancelling, strategically it is two weak forecasts cancelling — but the bilateral differential is close to zero in both cases.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Moderate-to-high risk-proxy pair: the quote leg is a designated haven and the base leg a commodity currency, so risk appetite transmits through both legs in the same direction and amplifies rather than cancels. Left at default strategically because the quote dossier's own conclusion is that a VIX at its 2026 low cannot be extrapolated over six months.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: CAD/CHF is a genuine risk-appetite pair, and the current regime is about as supportive as it gets. The base leg is a commodity currency whose USD cross carries a −0.2 to −0.3 correlation to the S&P 500; the quote leg is the G10's zero-rate haven and the funding leg of choice whenever volatility is compressed. Because the two legs sit on opposite sides of the risk trade, the pair's beta is the sum rather than the difference of their individual betas — the amplification case, and why the weight is raised. The cross-asset evidence is unambiguous: VIX closed at 14.51 on 2026-08-27, down 3.70 points over a month and having touched a 2026 low of 14.2, US high-yield OAS is 263bp having tightened 21bp on the month, investment grade is at 79bp, and the S&P 500 is at 7,670-7,712 near record levels. Two complications temper confidence rather than reversing it: the base leg's risk beta has partially decoupled because oil is rising on supply constraint rather than demand, and gold at 4,456 (+8.60% on the month) is the franc's traditional correlate being bought hard while the franc itself is sold, which is haven demand rotating to gold rather than disappearing.

S&P 500 7,670-7,712 near record levels; TSX Composite −1.02% on 2026-08-31 on tariff-specific Canadian pressure

Gold 4,456.44 (+8.60% one month, +22.39% one year) — the franc's correlate rising while the franc is sold
tactical.what_is_priced: The market is priced for a benign risk regime and is paying nothing for protection, with a VIX at the 2026 low and equities at records while the Strait of Hormuz remains contested; the pair earns its risk beta today from an entry point where the risk premium is compressed rather than cheap.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months this factor stops being a direction and becomes a distribution, and the distribution is not symmetric for this pair. Credit and equity volatility are close to the tight end of their post-2022 ranges, mechanically leaving far more room to widen than to compress, and CAD/CHF is convex in exactly the wrong direction for its carry: a risk shock hits the base leg through the commodity and growth channel and lifts the quote leg through the haven channel simultaneously. Both dossiers independently reached Neutral on strategic risk. Three named live catalysts sit inside the horizon: an unresolved Middle East conflict that has produced a Brent round trip from 100.31 to 88.24 and back above 90, a euro-area central bank tightening into an energy shock, and a Canadian tariff regime with no negotiating calendar. Against that, the franc's ability to capture a haven bid is genuinely impaired: gold has taken share, the yen has been outcompeting it with CHF/JPY down 2.61% over three months, and the SNB has stated twice since June that it has an increased willingness to intervene against rapid franc appreciation, truncating the right tail of any squeeze.

Brent round trip 100.31 (2026-07-24) to 88.24 (2026-08-25) to above 90 (2026-08-31) — unresolved supply risk on both legs

SNB stated increased willingness to intervene against rapid franc appreciation (2026-06-18, reaffirmed 2026-07-08)

strategic.what_is_priced: Markets price a continuation of the low-volatility, tight-credit regime across the full horizon, leaving no premium for the two live tails. For this pair the base leg's oil and risk channels now offset each other, so pricing affects the cost of hedging the tail rather than direction.

factors.horizon_split: Bullish to Neutral, and the mechanism is the difference between trading the level of risk appetite and trading its durability. Over four weeks a VIX at 14.51 and high-yield at 263bp mean the carry trade is rewarded and the pair's dual-sided beta works in its favour. Over six months the same compression is the reason the factor cannot be extrapolated, because there is far more room for volatility to rise than to fall and this pair is convex against a rise on both legs at once.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Speculators are short both legs, which the framework says mutes the pair signal — but the shorts are not remotely the same size, and the differential is what matters. On the base leg the combined leveraged-fund and asset-manager net short in Canadian dollar futures is 131,035 contracts as of the 2026-08-25 reference date, roughly 39.8% of the 329,544 open interest and around the 12th percentile of its trailing distribution, with 65,515 contracts covered in the fortnight to that date and dealers warehousing the other side at net long 124,930. On the quote leg the aggregate speculative net short is only 19.9k contracts at the 2026-08-28 release, roughly 18% of a 109,874 open interest and an estimated 48th percentile, with the covering run from −32.5k already spent. So the squeeze fuel is concentrated on the base leg by a factor of more than two on an open-interest-adjusted basis, and the marginal flow on the base leg is still covering while the quote leg has capacity to be re-shorted without hitting an extreme. Real-money flow reinforces it from a different direction: foreign investors bought a record C$80.8bn of Canadian government bonds in Q2 2026, an allocation decision arriving in the same quarter Canada's current account swung to surplus.

tactical.what_is_priced: Positioning is fuel rather than a price, and the bilateral read is that there is materially more of it under the base leg than the quote leg — base-leg covering came simultaneously from leveraged funds and asset managers while dealers reduced length, the profile of a genuine squeeze.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Strategically the two legs' positioning stories offset almost exactly, and the offset is structural rather than coincidental. On the base leg a residual 131,035-contract speculative short is a cushion under the Canadian dollar, but open interest has fallen 9.5% from 364,104 on 2026-08-11 and the leveraged-fund leg at −72,092 has dropped inside the −80,000 threshold the base dossier identifies as significant, so the tradeable extreme has partly resolved and a shrinking open-interest base weakens the squeeze mechanics. On the quote leg the strategically important number is the asset-manager short of −38,322 contracts observed 2026-08-11 — concentrated, slow-moving real money against a total open interest of only 109,874, precisely the configuration that has historically produced violent franc squeezes. That short is squeeze fuel pointing the other way for this pair. The honest netting is that each leg carries a crowded position whose unwind would move the pair in the opposite direction, both triggers exogenous and undated. Structural hedging flow is a further mild offset: Canadian pension funds create mechanical CAD demand when foreign asset values rise, while Switzerland's committed USD 200bn of outbound investment over five years is a genuine franc-negative capital outflow.

factors.horizon_split: Bullish to Neutral. Tactically the comparison is of flow and of extremity, and on both measures the base leg is more heavily and more actively short — 39.8% of open interest at the 12th percentile against 18% at an estimated 48th percentile. Strategically the comparison is of stock and of fragility, and there the quote leg's concentrated −38,322-contract real-money short becomes the more dangerous position for this pair, offsetting the base-leg cushion almost exactly.

tactical.combined_positioning_signal: Specs are short both legs, so the pair signal is muted in absolute terms but clearly positive in relative terms: 131,035 contracts of base-leg short at roughly the 12th percentile and 39.8% of open interest against 19.9k of quote-leg short at an estimated 48th percentile and 18% of open interest. The implied pair position is not extreme; the implied base-leg position is.
tactical.unwind_trigger: For the pair to be squeezed lower, the quote leg's short must be forced to cover — the credible tactical triggers are the SNB dropping or softening its intervention language at the 2026-09-24 assessment, a Middle East re-escalation that reverses the Brent decline, or an ECB that hikes on 2026-09-10 and explicitly signals it is finished. For the pair to be squeezed higher, the base leg's remaining short must cover, which a dovish Bank of Canada press conference on 2026-09-02 or a soft Fed outcome would do.
tactical.historical_analogue: The base leg's speculative short reached comparable extremes in early 2025 during the first tariff cycle and took roughly five months to normalise, trading a wide range rather than trending. The quote leg's analogue is the January 2015 floor removal, when a comparably one-sided structural short produced a violent single-session repricing — the cautionary case for this pair rather than the base case.
tactical.contrarian_case: The crowd may be right about the base leg: a currency facing 50% tariffs with no expiry and a central bank pinned at 2.25% deserves to be shorted, and a third of that short has already covered. And the pair's own positioning is not extreme, so buying it here is buying a consensus carry trade rather than a contrarian one — the honest characterisation is that positioning supports the trade mildly and does not initiate it.

strategic.combined_positioning_signal: Two crowded shorts pointing in opposite directions for the pair, both slow-moving and both held against long dealer books. The base leg is a cushion of diminishing potency; the quote leg is concentrated real-money squeeze fuel. Net signal: neutral, with the tail risk on the pair's downside.
strategic.unwind_trigger: The dated circuit-breaker for the base leg is the 2026-11-03 US midterms, which Ottawa itself expects to precede any substantive talks. The quote leg has no dated trigger, only an exogenous set: Middle East escalation, European credit stress as the ECB tightens into an energy shock, or a Fed cut that collapses the dollar leg of every carry trade at once.
strategic.historical_analogue: Funding-currency shorts of this structure unwind violently and rarely on schedule. The relevant precedent for the pair is not a CAD event but a CHF event: the January 2015 SNB floor removal, moderated by the fact that the SNB now holds CHF 889.6bn of official reserve assets and has stated it will lean against rapid appreciation, which caps magnitude without changing direction.
strategic.contrarian_case: The contrarian case against a long CAD/CHF over six months is that the pair is the crowd's favourite carry vehicle at a point when the crowd is short both legs and the option surface charges almost nothing for the scenario that resolves it. That is not a reason to be short the pair — the carry accrues either way — but it is the reason positioning cannot be scored bullish strategically.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both economies posted record external prints inside the tactical window, which is an unusual configuration and produces a genuine standoff. Canada's current account swung from a C$8.3bn deficit in Q1 to a C$8.8bn surplus in Q2 — the first since 2022 and the largest since 2005 — against a C$3.5bn consensus, driven by record energy and auto exports, with June total exports at a record C$77.5bn. Switzerland's July trade surplus widened to CHF 8.1bn, the largest since the series began in January 1950, on exports up 13.8% and imports down 4.5%. On the delta, Canada's improvement is the larger and faster; on the level, Switzerland is far ahead. The terms-of-trade channel is where the bilateral tilt actually lives, and it is oil: Brent at 90.135 and WTI at 85.446 is a direct revenue transfer to the base leg, explicitly carved out of the Section 338 tariff regime, and a direct cost to the quote leg, a net energy importer. Gold cuts the other way and hard: Switzerland is the world's largest refining hub and gold is up 8.60% on the month. Bilateral goods trade between the two is small and near-balanced, so direct trade flow is not a driver either way.

tactical.what_is_priced: Neither record is priced, for opposite reasons: Canada's surplus is dismissed as an oil artefact and Switzerland's is treated as permanent wallpaper that never surprises. With the mirror-image commodity exposures roughly cancelling, there is no identifiable four-week mispricing in the external channel.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.16 strategic weight this is the largest single counterweight to the carry case, and it runs against the pair. The level differential is not close: Switzerland runs a current account of 9.77% of GDP with a net international investment position of CHF 974bn, roughly 120% of annual output, thrown off by a goods surplus in pharmaceuticals and precision engineering, a services surplus in financial and commodity-trading revenue, and a large primary income surplus. Canada's Q2 surplus of C$8.8bn is roughly 1.1% of quarterly GDP and reverses a decade of small deficits — a genuine improvement, and still eight percentage points of GDP behind. That gap is a continuous, price-insensitive excess of franc receipts over franc payments that must be repatriated, hedged or absorbed by the official sector, and it is the mechanism by which the Swiss real effective exchange rate has trended higher for decades despite paying nothing. Structural concentration compounds it: roughly 70% of Canadian exports go to a single increasingly hostile customer, with duties escalating on 2027-01-01, while the WCS-WTI heavy differential of about US$12/bbl caps Canadian realisation of any Brent rally. The offsets are real and are why confidence is 62 rather than higher — Swiss pharma faces Section 232 tariffs of up to 15%, Switzerland's Q1 current account was already CHF 11bn below year-ago levels, and the USD 200bn outbound investment commitment is a material franc-negative capital flow — but none of them closes an eight-point-of-GDP gap.

A near-10%-of-GDP surplus puts a floor under the quote leg that a 225bp carry deficit does not break — precisely why the strategic net score sits inside the Neutral band.

factors.horizon_split: Neutral to Bearish, and the weight almost triples from 0.06 to 0.16, so this factor's contribution goes from nothing to the largest single negative in the strategic score. Over four weeks two record prints and two mirror-image commodity exposures cancel, while over six months the arithmetic of a 9.77%-of-GDP surplus against a near-balanced position becomes the binding constraint on how far the pair can rise on carry alone.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: Canada — crude oil and natural gas the dominant exposures, with WTI at 85.446 and Brent at 90.135 on 2026-08-31; also potash, critical minerals and aluminium. Energy, potash, fish and critical minerals are explicitly carved out of the 50% Section 338 tariff regime. Realisation is capped by a WCS-WTI heavy differential of roughly US$12/bbl.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: Switzerland — no commodity export base, so exposure runs through two channels only: net energy importer (higher crude/gas is a terms-of-trade cost), and the world's largest gold refining hub, with gold at 4,456.44 (+8.60% month, +22.39% year) franc-supportive through both refining and the shared safe-haven channel.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Applying the framework's direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: ++CAD on the base leg through export revenue with the tariff carve-out intact, and a mild negative on the quote leg through the net-importer channel — pair UP, structurally long oil. Natural gas up: negative for the quote leg as an importer, positive for the base leg as an LNG and gas exporter — same direction, pair UP. Gold up: neutral-to-mildly-positive for the base leg, +CHF for the quote leg through the safe-haven correlation and refining hub — pair DOWN. Netting the three at current levels: crude has round-tripped from 100.31 to 88.24 and back above 90, roughly flat over the month, while gold has risen 8.60% over the same month — the gold leg has been the stronger of the two and the net commodity impulse over the trailing month is mildly PAIR-NEGATIVE, even though the pair's structural commodity beta is clearly pair-positive. This is the single most important netting result in the analysis and it is why Factor 5 is Neutral tactically rather than Bullish.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Brent from roughly 90 to 99. Base leg gains materially through tariff-exempt energy export revenue, extending the current-account surplus. Quote leg loses mildly as a net importer, and euro-area inflation pressure would push the ECB toward further tightening, weakening the franc. Net: clearly pair-positive, in the order of 1-2% before any risk-off offset — the sign flips above roughly US$110 where the haven bid on the quote leg and the global growth hit to the base leg dominate.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Brent from roughly 90 to 81. Base leg loses its terms-of-trade support, Canadian headline CPI converges down and the market's roughly 65% probability of a 2026 Bank of Canada hike loses its statistical basis — a double hit through revenue and rates. Quote leg gains as a net importer. Net: clearly pair-negative, the more dangerous of the two directions because it removes both Canadian pillars at once.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Crude oil, by a wide margin, because it is the only commodity acting on both legs simultaneously and in opposite directions. Gold is the meaningful secondary driver and the one currently working against the pair, unusual in that it is the quote leg's commodity exposure and has been the stronger impulse over the trailing month; the August pickup in Swiss inflation partly reflected higher petroleum costs and the weaker franc pushing up prices for imported goods.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The two central banks give guidance of completely different kinds, and the asymmetry favours the pair. The SNB does not publish a rate path but in June gave something more directional: an explicitly one-sided statement of its exchange-rate reaction function, saying it has an increased willingness to intervene in the foreign exchange market to counter a rapid and excessive appreciation of the franc, reaffirmed by Chairman Schlegel on 2026-07-08. There is no corresponding commitment against franc weakness, and no plausible level of depreciation at which a bank forecasting 0.6% inflation would object — a written option against the quote leg strengthening, backed by CHF 889.6bn of official reserve assets. The Bank of Canada is two-sided by construction: the July statement judged the current rate appropriate while stating uncertainty is still high, and the Summary of Deliberations disclosed an explicit range of views among Governing Council members. Sequence matters inside the window and favours the pair: the Bank of Canada speaks first on 2026-09-02, where a hold is universally expected and only tone is tradeable, and the SNB follows on 2026-09-24 with a quarterly projection round where the operative question is not the rate but whether the intervention sentence survives.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market prices both decisions as holds and prices the SNB's intervention language as a permanent feature rather than a live variable, while pricing the Bank of Canada's tone as a coin flip. The unpriced item is the SNB sentence itself, after the franc depreciated 3.39% against the euro over six months.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months both central banks' guidance points the same way — toward a weaker home currency — so the factor becomes a comparison of which reaction function binds harder, and it is the SNB's. The quote leg's structural incentive to prefer a soft franc has strengthened: Swiss pharmaceutical exporters now face Section 232 tariffs of up to 15%, raising the SNB's sensitivity to further competitiveness loss, with two quarterly projection rounds inside the horizon at which the rate is near-certain to remain at zero. On the base leg the guidance wedge runs the other way: the market carries roughly 65% probability of a 2026 Bank of Canada hike against the Bank's own Q2 Market Participants Survey median of 2.25% through January 2027, and the 2026-10-28 decision — the one date carrying a Monetary Policy Report — is where the Bank must mark down both growth and inflation. That repricing is worth 15 to 20bp on the Canadian two-year and is a genuine pair-negative. What keeps the net positive is durability: the Canadian wedge is a one-off repricing at a dated event, while the SNB's cap is a standing condition restated at 2026-09-24 and again at 2026-12-10.

strategic.what_is_priced: Consensus prices an SNB that tolerates and quietly welcomes franc weakness, which is correct, and a Bank of Canada more likely to hike than to cut, which we think is too hawkish. The market is treating the SNB's asymmetric option as a two-way commitment, which it provides no support for if the base leg's rate story deteriorates.

factors.horizon_split: Bullish on both horizons with confidence falling from 58 to 52 as the weight rises from 0.07 to 0.12. Tactically the sequence helps — the Bank of Canada's non-event comes first and the SNB's projection round second, with a standing cap on franc strength intact. Strategically the 2026-10-28 Monetary Policy Report introduces a dated, specific and falsifiable pair-negative on the base leg that has no equivalent on the quote leg, which compresses the net advantage without reversing it.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Severely asymmetric bilateral event risk: the base leg faces a 50% tariff regime imposed under an authority with no expiry, no negotiating calendar and a dated escalation, while the quote leg's principal event exposure is a referendum polling 62-36 against.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Event risk is the clearest pair-negative in the tactical window and the asymmetry is not close. On the base leg, Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect on 2026-09-08 on approximately US$20bn of US imports at 15-50% covering steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, electronics and motorcycles, and the product-level list was unpublished at the valuation date — an unpriced binary inside the window. It follows the 2026-08-22 imposition of 50% US duties under Section 338 on approximately US$20bn of Canadian goods across 554 tariff lines, the first presidential use of that authority since 1949, applied regardless of USMCA preference and carrying no expiry date, with the USTR confirming no new talks are planned. Prime Minister Carney's own framing was that Canada had been attacked. On the quote leg the dated item is the 2026-09-27 federal referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality, which August Tamedia/20 Minuten polling has at 62% against and 36% in favour, so rejection is the strong base case and the modal outcome a non-event; the quote leg's other exposure, Section 232 pharma tariffs of up to 15% and a variable Section 301 headline rate of up to 12.5% with MFN credit, is materially milder in rate and already effective. Transmission compounds the asymmetry: the Middle East conflict that is live on both sides is the one shock that hits the base leg through growth and the quote leg through haven demand at the same time, so its tail is pair-negative twice over.

tactical.what_is_priced: Very little is priced on either leg. The store's own volatility surface runs 5.138% at 38.6 days, 5.271% at 94.7 and 5.388% at 185.7 — a clean contango with no near-term kink across a September containing five separate event dates. The date and headline amount of the 2026-09-08 retaliation are known; its sector composition and the probability of further US escalation are not.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Strategically the base leg's event risk stops being a series of dates and becomes a structural condition, which is what makes this the highest-confidence negative in the analysis. Section 338 permits proclamation-only tariffs with no prior investigation and carries no time limit, so unlike the IEEPA tariffs struck down in February 2026 the duties remain until a future presidential proclamation removes them — there is no statutory clock forcing the parties back to the table. Ottawa's own assessment is that no substantive talks resume before the 2026-11-03 midterms, Carney has told premiers that industry support will remain beyond the life of the current US administration, and the escalation path is already announced: duties on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts and steel rise to 50% on 2027-01-01, striking the sector that drove Q2 growth. The USMCA architecture that would normally constrain this was triggered for review on 2026-07-01 with Canada absent from the parallel US-Mexico track. The quote leg's strategic event set is milder and slower: Bilaterals III was signed on 2026-03-02 and is progressing through ratification with clear stakeholder support, UBS concentration risk is real but undated, and the pharma tariff regime is a growth rather than a solvency threat. The pair's convexity is decisive: every high-magnitude scenario in the horizon moves the base leg down and the quote leg up simultaneously.

strategic.what_is_priced: The market has priced the tariff headline and not the tariff duration, and it has priced the pair's shared geopolitical tail at nothing: an estimated 5.388% at 185.7 days is a low absolute level of volatility for a cross whose base leg faces a permanent escalating tariff regime and whose quote leg is the developed world's convexity trade.

factors.horizon_split: Bearish on both horizons with confidence rising from 62 to 68. The tactical risk is the unpublished composition of the 2026-09-08 retaliation list, a bounded uncertainty resolved within days. The strategic risk is the absence of any mechanism to end the regime, compounded by a dated escalation on 2027-01-01 that sits just beyond the strategic window but is priced inside it. Duration, not magnitude, is what makes the longer horizon the stronger case.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is a AAA-versus-AAA pair and nothing is scheduled, so Neutral is a deliberate assessment rather than a placeholder. Canada is rated AAA by Standard & Poor's, Aaa by Moody's and AAA by DBRS with AA+ from Fitch, making it one of only two AAA-rated G7 sovereigns; Switzerland is AAA from every major agency, reconfirmed by Morningstar DBRS with a Stable trend on 2026-01-16. Neither faces a rating action, review or auction stress inside the tactical window. Both are, if anything, receiving positive marginal news: Canada's budget balance printed +0.99 at the 2026-08-28 release against a −0.31 prior, and record foreign purchases of C$80.8bn of Canadian government bonds in Q2 are the opposite of supply indigestion; Switzerland's fiscal balance was an estimated surplus of 0.4% of GDP in 2025 under a constitutional debt brake. Neither differential is capable of moving a currency in four weeks. The one live tactical consideration is that Canada's tariff support package is explicitly open-ended and unbudgeted, so any costing announced around the 2026-09-08 retaliation date would be a new base-leg fiscal datapoint — low probability, and not enough to move a AAA sovereign inside a month.

tactical.what_is_priced: Nothing fiscal is priced into this cross at this horizon and nothing should be. Two AAA sovereigns with improving balances and no scheduled events generate no tradeable signal over four weeks, and the confidence of 58 reflects the reliability of that no-signal conclusion rather than conviction in a direction.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the comparison becomes relative rather than absolute, and on a relative basis the quote leg is the stronger sovereign — modestly, but the direction is not ambiguous. Switzerland runs a structural surplus averaging around 0.2% of GDP to 2028 under a constitutional debt brake, with gross debt somewhere between 30% and 41% of GDP depending on measure, and no bond supply story at all. Canada's position is excellent in G7 terms, with the lowest net debt-to-GDP in the group, a deficit revised down to C$66.9bn and record foreign demand for its curve, but it is a deficit rather than a surplus, the federal ratio is rising toward 43% before stabilising, and the tariff support package Carney has committed to is explicitly open-ended and unbudgeted against a shrinking tariff-exposed tax base. Provincial dynamics diverge sharply, with Ontario and Quebec carrying both the larger deficits and the larger tariff exposure. The transmission to the pair is slow and diffuse — a quality preference on the quote leg cannot be expressed through a 0.31% ten-year, so it has to be expressed through the currency, which is the weaker channel — and that is why confidence is 50 rather than higher.

strategic.what_is_priced: The market prices both sovereigns as non-issues and prices no relative-quality premium into the cross. The quote leg's twin-surplus position against a base leg running a deficit with an uncapped contingent commitment is a slow, unglamorous bid for the franc that consensus does not account for — small enough to size at a 0.07 weight, real enough not to score zero.

factors.horizon_split: Neutral to Bearish. Tactically there is no scheduled fiscal event on either leg and two AAA sovereigns generate no impulse. Strategically fiscal quality only expresses itself through relative comparison over time, and over six months a Swiss structural surplus under a debt brake against a Canadian deficit with an open-ended and unbudgeted tariff-support commitment is a genuine if slow-moving differential in the quote leg's favour.

catalysts.rationale: The rate outcome was a non-event with a 3% hike probability priced and all 35 Reuters-polled economists forecasting a hold at 2.25%, so the bilateral differential is unchanged either way. The tradeable content was tone, and the outcome was mildly pair-positive: the Bank held at 2.25% and its recognition of a broadening recovery and increased inflation risks gave the decision a mildly hawkish tilt. The pair set its 52-week intraday and closing highs that session.

catalysts.event: Swiss detailed Q2 GDP release and August CPI
catalysts.rationale: This catalyst has already fired and it fired against the pair. Q2 GDP expanded 1.9%, the strongest quarterly growth in five years and above the 1.6% consensus, while CPI rose 0.4% month-on-month and 0.8% year-on-year, and core CPI also surprised to the upside at 0.4% against a 0.3% consensus. The pair closed 17 pips lower on the day. Transmission is not through the current policy rate but through the tail probability that the SNB's zero-rate commitment is eventually abandoned earlier than June 2027.

catalysts.event: Canada Labour Force Survey and Ivey PMI, plus the CFTC Commitments of Traders release
catalysts.rationale: Consensus is +15.8k employment with unemployment steady at 6.4% after July's +75.1k, sustaining the base leg's rate support. The same day's positioning print is the first read on whether the base leg's 131,035-contract speculative short keeps covering. A soft US ADP print (38,000 new private-sector jobs, weakest since January) is dollar-negative, the worst quadrant for the franc per the quote dossier.

catalysts.event: Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect on approximately US$20bn of US goods at 15-50%
catalysts.rationale: The product-level list was unpublished at the valuation date, an unpriced binary on the base leg inside the tactical window. Dollar-for-dollar retaliation by an economy roughly one tenth the size of its counterpart is proportionally heavier on Canada. Transmission is through the base leg's growth channel with no offsetting quote-leg effect, unambiguously pair-negative; mitigated by the base leg already having absorbed the larger 2026-08-22 shock without the pair breaking its uptrend.

catalysts.event: Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index for August
catalysts.rationale: The most important base-leg data point of the tactical window. Priors are headline 3.0%, CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%. If CPI-trim rises toward 2.2% the differential gains a path to 250bp; if it slips below 1.9% the statistical basis for a 2026 hike disappears. The same global petroleum impulse that would lift Canadian headline CPI also drove Swiss August inflation, making this print less differentiating than it looks.

July produced a CHF 8.1bn surplus, the largest since the series began in January 1950, on chemical and pharmaceutical exports up 25.7%. A second consecutive record would strengthen the quote leg's structural bid; a sharp fall would confirm July was Section 232 front-running that reverses inside the strategic window, weakening that offset and being pair-positive.

catalysts.event: SNB quarterly monetary policy assessment with a refreshed conditional inflation forecast
catalysts.rationale: The single largest binary in the tactical window. A hold at 0.00% is effectively certain, so the entire tradeable content is the language: the June statement's increased willingness to intervene against rapid and excessive franc appreciation was written when the franc was under upward pressure, and after a 3.39% six-month depreciation against the euro that pressure has abated. Dropping or softening the sentence would be read as tolerance of a stronger franc and is the clearest identified pair-negative in the window. The August CPI surprise raises the stakes on the forecast itself.

catalysts.event: Swiss federal referendum on constitutionally entrenching neutrality
catalysts.rationale: Passage would bar Switzerland from joining sanctions against belligerent states absent a UN Security Council mandate and constrain NATO cooperation. August polling has 62% against and 36% in favour, so rejection is the strong base case and the modal outcome is a non-event for the pair. The tail cuts both ways for the quote leg, which is why the expected impact is Neutral rather than directional.

Core Swiss inflation rose for the first time this year in August, to 0.4%, and a second consecutive rise would begin to pull SNB hike pricing inside its currently comfortable June 2027 position — the single cleanest mechanism by which the +225bp differential that carries 47% of the tactical score starts to erode. A reversion to 0.3% core restores the status quo and is pair-neutral.

catalysts.event: Bank of Canada decision with Monetary Policy Report
catalysts.rationale: The most important dated event of the strategic horizon and the identified inflection between the two stances. The Bank must publish a full forecast round incorporating post-tariff activity data, marking down 2026 growth for the tariff shock while marking down inflation as gasoline base effects roll off. National Bank and Scotiabank forecast a hike to 2.50%, strongly pair-positive; BMO, CIBC, RBC and TD forecast a hold, in which case the roughly 65% year-end hike premium comes out of the Canadian curve.

The only dated circuit-breaker for the base leg's tariff conflict inside the strategic horizon; Ottawa's own assessment is that no substantive talks resume before it. The mechanism is indirect and slow — US domestic political pressure from tariff-driven cost-of-living pain — but a credible restart would reprice the base leg's entire tariff risk premium in a single move, since Section 338 duties are removable by proclamation with no statutory process.

The final base-leg decision of 2026 and the terminal date for the market's roughly 65% year-end hike probability. National Bank and Scotiabank forecast 2.75% by this meeting, a cumulative 50bp of tightening taking the bilateral differential to 275bp; the other four large Canadian banks forecast 2.25%. If the Bank has not moved by this date the entire 2026 hike premium is removed from the Canadian curve.

catalysts.event: SNB quarterly monetary policy assessment with a refreshed conditional inflation forecast
catalysts.rationale: The final quote-leg assessment of 2026, arriving one day after the Bank of Canada. With the rate all but certain to remain at 0.00%, the variables are the intervention language and any revision to the 2027-2028 conditional forecast path. A retained cap plus an unchanged forecast extends the carry structure; a softened cap or a forecast revision bringing the first hike inside 2027 would be pair-negative and, after August's core surprise, is more plausible than a month ago.

The largest recurring dollar-funding squeeze in the calendar and the most reliable seasonal source of cross-currency basis widening. Because the quote leg is the funding currency of the trade this pair expresses, a basis widening forces carry positions to be reduced, which is mechanically a bid for the franc and therefore pair-negative. With the three-month EUR/USD basis last observed at only −16 to −20bp, there is more room than usual for it to widen, and the effect should be larger than usual given the size of the franc-funded book documented in the Positioning section.

catalysts.event: United States tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts and steel rise to 50%
catalysts.rationale: A dated, pre-announced escalation that extends the base leg's tariff regime beyond the current US$20bn and 5.2% of bilateral exports to a materially larger share, striking the auto sector that drove Q2 GDP growth with a 27.0% annualised export surge. Section 338 carries no expiry, so the escalation persists until a presidential proclamation removes it. It sits just beyond the strategic window but is priced inside it, and there is no quote-leg equivalent.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with staff projections
catalysts.rationale: A 25bp hike to a 2.50% deposit rate is close to fully priced and would take the euro-franc policy spread from 225bp to 250bp, the single largest mechanical driver of quote-leg weakness in the CHF dossier, reaching this pair by read-across. The tradeable content is the guidance: an explicit signal that the cycle is complete would collapse the euro terminal-rate premium and is the most likely source of a franc rally in September, which would be pair-negative.

catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: Neither leg is the dollar, so transmission is through the vehicle-currency and dollar-smile channels that Factor 10 scores. One reading gives a 58% probability of a hike after Jackson Hole, firming the dollar and deepening the carry regime that favours this pair; another reading gives a genuinely two-sided distribution in which a cut collapses the dollar leg of every carry trade at once. The bilateral evidence points to the hawkish read holding for now, per the franc trading near its lowest since 19 August on Chair Warsh's remarks.

invalidators.condition: SNB removes or materially softens the 'increased willingness to intervene' formulation at the 2026-09-24 or 2026-12-10 assessment
invalidators.mechanism: The pair's downside cap is a written option against quote-leg strength that Factors 6 and 3 both lean on — its removal converts an asymmetric policy constraint into a two-way market and, on the quote dossier's own estimate, is worth 100-150 pips on EUR/CHF and a comparable 60-90 pips on this cross given its lower beta to the euro leg.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: SNB monetary policy assessment statement text, specifically the presence of any reference to countering franc appreciation
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Quarterly, at the two scheduled assessments

invalidators.condition: CAD/CHF closes below 0.57811 for two consecutive sessions
invalidators.mechanism: 0.57811 is the lower edge of the two-touch shelf the pair cleared in mid-August, and below it the next computed support is the three-touch 0.57167-0.57617 band — a break would end the unbroken sequence of higher swing lows running from 0.56511 on 3 July through 0.58447 on 3 September, the only price-structure evidence that the carry trade is being expressed rather than merely available.

invalidators.condition: The bilateral policy differential narrows below 200bp — a Bank of Canada cut to 2.00% or an SNB hike to 0.25%
invalidators.mechanism: Factor 1 supplies +0.1485 of a +0.0291 strategic score, so a 25bp compression alone moves the net score to approximately −0.01 and a differential below 200bp with a deteriorating trajectory takes it decisively negative. The realistic route is a Canadian cut forced by tariff drag, since the SNB leg is remote (swaps curve fully prices a first 25bp hike only in June 2027).
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Bank of Canada overnight rate target and SNB policy rate; Canadian OIS-implied path
invalidators.monitor_frequency: At each of the five scheduled decisions in the horizon

invalidators.condition: Swiss core CPI prints at or above 0.6% year-on-year for two consecutive months
invalidators.mechanism: Would pull market pricing of the first SNB hike inside 2027 and attack the pair's carry premise at its only vulnerable end. August already delivered the first core increase of the year, to 0.4% from 0.3%, and the pickup partly reflected the weaker franc pushing up imported goods prices — a self-limiting mechanism for a rising pair, since further CAD/CHF appreciation imports more Swiss inflation.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Federal Statistical Office core CPI, next release 2026-10-01

invalidators.condition: Brent crude closes below US$75 for two consecutive weekly closes
invalidators.mechanism: The framework's netting rules make this pair structurally long oil on both legs at once: the base leg loses tariff-exempt export revenue and the statistical basis for its roughly 65% 2026 hike pricing simultaneously, while the quote leg gains as a net energy importer. It is the only single variable that damages both legs of the bull case in the same move.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: ICE Brent front-month settlement against US$75.00, currently 90.135

invalidators.condition: Gold rises a further 15% while Brent is unchanged or lower
invalidators.mechanism: The net commodity impulse for this pair would become decisively negative: gold is the quote leg's commodity exposure through the world's largest refining hub and the shared safe-haven channel, it has already risen 8.60% in a month against a round-tripping crude price, and Factor 5's netting result is that the gold leg has recently been the stronger of the two.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: XAU/USD against roughly 5,125, currently 4,456.44, alongside Brent

invalidators.condition: VIX closes above 25 or US high-yield OAS widens beyond 350bp for three consecutive sessions
invalidators.mechanism: This pair's risk beta is additive rather than offsetting — the base leg is a commodity currency and the quote leg the designated haven — and the franc-funded carry book documented in the Positioning section would be forced to unwind into a dealer community already long both legs at +124,930 and +62,382 contracts.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CBOE VIX against 25.0 (currently 14.51) and ICE BofA US High Yield OAS against 3.50% (currently 2.63%)

invalidators.condition: CFTC base-leg combined speculative net short falls inside 60,000 contracts from 131,035 while CAD/CHF fails to make a new high
invalidators.mechanism: The squeeze fuel that Factor 4 scores at 39.8% of open interest and the 12th percentile would be materially exhausted without having delivered a price payoff — the signature of a squeeze that has been monetised rather than one still running.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CFTC Traders in Financial Futures, Canadian dollar leveraged-fund plus asset-manager net
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Weekly, Friday release with a Tuesday reference date

signposts.indicator: Bilateral policy rate differential (BoC minus SNB)
signposts.current_level: +225bp (Bank of Canada 2.25% as of 2026-08-31; SNB 0.00% as of 2026-09-01)
signposts.confirms_if: Widens to 250bp on a Bank of Canada hike at 2026-10-28 or 2026-12-09, or holds at 225bp with Canadian year-end hike probability above 50%
signposts.invalidates_if: Narrows below 200bp on a Canadian cut, or market pricing of a first SNB hike moves inside December 2026
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the only factor in the analysis whose evidence is arithmetic rather than judgement, and at an applied weight of 0.27 it supplies 47% of the tactical positive score and 100% of the strategic positive bloc net of Guidance. It is the single widest positive differential available to the base leg anywhere in the G10, measured against the only zero rate in the set.
signposts.frequency: At each of the three Bank of Canada and two SNB decisions inside the horizon

signposts.indicator: Market-implied timing of the first SNB rate hike
signposts.current_level: June 2027 on the swaps curve; early 2028 on the economist consensus
signposts.confirms_if: Stays at June 2027 or later through the horizon
signposts.invalidates_if: Moves inside March 2027, or any material probability attaches to a 2026 move
signposts.bilateral_importance: The quote leg's rate is the immovable half of the differential — the base leg's path is genuinely two-sided with the six largest Canadian banks split four to two — so the pair's carry premise depends more on this signpost holding than on anything the Bank of Canada does.
signposts.frequency: Daily for market pricing; monthly on each Swiss CPI release

signposts.current_level: 0.4% in August 2026, up from 0.3% — the first increase this year, against headline of 0.8%
signposts.confirms_if: Reverts to 0.3% or below on the 2026-10-01 release, restoring the four-month run of 0.3% prints
signposts.invalidates_if: Prints at or above 0.6% for two consecutive months
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the pair's self-limiting mechanism and matters far more here than for the franc in isolation: a rising CAD/CHF imports Swiss inflation through the exchange-rate channel, so the pair's own advance generates the data that would eventually remove its carry.
signposts.frequency: Monthly, first business days; next release 2026-10-01

signposts.indicator: CFTC speculative net positioning, both legs
signposts.current_level: Base leg (CAD) combined leveraged-fund plus asset-manager net short 131,035 contracts, 39.8% of 329,544 open interest, roughly 12th percentile; quote leg (CHF) aggregate net short 19.9k contracts, roughly 18% of 109,874 open interest, estimated 48th percentile
signposts.confirms_if: The base-leg short continues shrinking while the quote-leg short rebuilds beyond 25,000 contracts
signposts.invalidates_if: The base-leg short falls inside 60,000 contracts without a new pair high, or the quote-leg short covers to better than 12,000 contracts
signposts.bilateral_importance: Neither leg's net is extreme in isolation; the ratio is, and only a bilateral reading sees it. A base-leg short at the 12th percentile against a quote-leg short at the 48th is the entire content of Factor 4's tactical Bullish.
signposts.frequency: Weekly, Friday release covering the prior Tuesday

signposts.indicator: Franc funding-currency adoption versus the yen
signposts.current_level: Franc short positioning at a two-month high while yen shorts have been halved over a fortnight; Swiss rates 0% against Japanese rates 1%
signposts.confirms_if: The rotation continues — franc shorts extend while yen shorts stay reduced, and CHF/JPY continues to fall
signposts.invalidates_if: The rotation reverses on Swiss inflation firming, or a franc squeeze forces the accumulated funding book to unwind
signposts.bilateral_importance: This is the flow neither dossier contains and it is pair-specific in a way that positioning data alone is not. CAD/CHF is a direct beneficiary because it is a high-carry cross whose funding leg is the currency being adopted; the same rotation does nothing for CAD/JPY.
signposts.frequency: Weekly on CFTC data; continuous on CHF/JPY

signposts.current_level: US$90.135 on 2026-08-31, having round-tripped from US$100.31 to US$88.24
signposts.confirms_if: Holds a US$85-100 range, sustaining the base leg's tariff-exempt export revenue and the quote leg's imported-inflation headwind
signposts.invalidates_if: Falls below US$75 for two consecutive weekly closes, or spikes above US$110, at which point the haven bid on the quote leg dominates the revenue transfer
signposts.bilateral_importance: Oil is the only commodity acting on both legs of this pair simultaneously and in opposite directions, so its net effect on CAD/CHF is roughly double its effect on either currency's trade-weighted index; it is also the variable with a sign flip.

signposts.indicator: CAD/CHF position relative to 0.58783 and the 0.58738-0.6182 structural void
signposts.current_level: Spot 0.58554, sixteen pips below the two-touch 0.58684-0.58738 resistance band and 229 pips below the void's upper boundary at 0.6182
signposts.confirms_if: Three consecutive daily closes above 0.58783, the 52-week high, placing the pair in territory with no computed resistance for 5.2%
signposts.invalidates_if: A second failure at 0.58783 followed by a close below 0.57811
signposts.bilateral_importance: The void is a pair-specific structural fact with no analogue in either currency's trade-weighted chart, and it is the reason the tactical upside case is 50 pips larger than the downside case and therefore the reason the expected value is positive at all.

signposts.current_level: 6.29%, against 60-day of 5.31% and a store three-month at-the-money estimate of 5.271% (corrected range 5.7-6.2%)
signposts.confirms_if: Stays below 8%, keeping the carry-to-vol ratio above roughly 0.28 and the funding trade economic
signposts.invalidates_if: Sustains above 10%, at which point 225bp of carry against a double-digit volatility makes the position uneconomic regardless of direction
signposts.bilateral_importance: The strategic score of +0.029 is the sum of a +0.21 carry bloc and a −0.18 structural bloc, and the single variable that decides between them is realised volatility, because the carry bloc's value is entirely a function of the denominator.

assumptions: This is pass 2 of 2: the ten factor stances, confidences, evidence types, applied weights, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions, rationales, G10 rankings and cross-horizon assessment arrived settled from pass 1, which scored them without the price payload, and are carried verbatim without adjustment.

Pass 1's consensus arithmetic was corrected in this pass: crossing the five-bank USD/CAD forecast against the corroborated USD/CHF cluster implies a derived cross consensus roughly 60 pips below payload spot (mildly pair-negative), not above it as originally stated.

Two data points released after the 2026-09-01 valuation date (Swiss August CPI at 0.8% and Q2 GDP at its strongest in five years) push against the quote-leg half of the thesis; neither moves the SNB inside either horizon but the direction of surprise on the quote leg has turned.

The payload spot date (2026-09-03) is two trading sessions after the 2026-09-01 valuation date; every level, target, pip figure and distance-to-average in this report is computed against the payload spot of 0.58554 rather than a fresher web quote.

All moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes computed over the whole stored history (4,879 weekday bars, 2007-12-24 to 2026-09-03), not over the 130 bars shown for the narrative; weekend bars never enter the store.

CAD/CHF has no listed option; the payload's at-the-money implied volatility figures are variance-identity estimates fed a realised correlation as a proxy for an unobservable implied one, documented to understate by 8.7-17.8% against direct quotes with a 14.4% median understatement across seventeen pairs — treated as a floor throughout and never presented as a dealer quote.
No 25-delta risk reversal is obtainable for this cross from any accessible source — a documented gap, not estimated.

Forward points and outrights are derived linearly from the store's futures calendar-spread premium (238.4bp annualised, observed 2026-08-31 over 14.6-105.7 days) and are a derivation rather than dealer quotes; cross-pair futures calendar-spread signs are contract-convention dependent so magnitude is used and sign is not.

The +311bp ten-year rate differential uses monthly series for both legs as of 2026-06-01, approximately 92 days old at the valuation date, breaching both the 30-day tactical and 60-day strategic freshness windows, and is never quoted as a live level.

No PPP conversion is available for this cross; the valuation read is constructed from the two legs' BIS real effective exchange rates (both June 2026, roughly 63 days from the valuation date) combined with the pair's own 52-week and 200-week positions, which point in opposite directions and are reported as such.

Bilateral trade figures are taken directly from the supplied IMF DOTS block for 2024 and not re-estimated; the mirror asymmetry between Canadian- and Swiss-reported bilateral trade is a known feature of Swiss trade statistics driven by non-monetary gold flows and is flagged rather than reconciled.

Several figures carried from the two underlying dossiers retain their originating staleness or sourcing caveats (Swiss July trade surplus, EUR/USD basis, Swiss referendum poll, CHF asset-manager short observation date, WCS-WTI differential) and are flagged individually in the relevant sections.
Weight adjustments (Factors 1, 2, 3 tactical, 7, 10) were set in pass 1 and are carried unchanged; all adjustments are within the framework's ±0.05 limit and both horizons sum to exactly 1.00.

Scenario probabilities, tail probabilities and invalidator probabilities are analyst judgements calibrated to the factor analysis and the payload's volatility, not derived from options-implied distributions, which do not exist for this cross.
